components.note: 扌 (hand) — 掩 describes covering or shutting something with the hand.
奄 (yǎn) gives the sound — an exact match with 掩.
羊 here pictures a woven lid or cover.
皿 (dish) sits below, together giving 盖 its meaning 'lid, to cover.'

example.hanzi: 厚厚的雪掩盖了整个山谷。
example.pinyin: Hòuhòu de xuě yǎngài le zhěnggè shāngǔ.
example.english: The thick snow covered the entire valley.
example.fact: The Chicxulub asteroid impact 66 million years ago threw up enough dust and soot to blanket the atmosphere for years, blocking sunlight and plunging the planet into darkness — a global cover-up of sunlight that scientists believe helped end the age of dinosaurs.

components.note: 宀 (a roofed building) — 官 named the hall where court officials carried out state business.
The lower element traces back to a heap or mound shape, suggesting many people gathered under that roof, reinforcing 官's meaning 'official, government post.'
司 depicts a person with a raised arm giving orders — an official directing others, giving rise to the meaning 'to manage' or 'to take charge of.'

example.hanzi: 他们为了这块地打了好几年官司。
example.pinyin: Tāmen wèile zhè kuài dì dǎle hǎo jǐ nián guānsi.
example.english: They fought a lawsuit over this piece of land for several years.
example.fact: The Code of Hammurabi, carved onto a stone stele around 1754 BC, is one of the oldest surviving sets of written laws, and it already included detailed rules for resolving property disputes and contracts — showing that formal legal proceedings are almost as old as writing itself.

meanings: Tonkin (northern Vietnam during the French colonial period)

components.note: 东 (simplified from 東) originally pictured the sun 日 rising behind a tree 木 — since the sun rises in the east, the character came to mean 'east.'
京 depicts a tall building raised on a hill or mound — ancient capitals were built on elevated ground for defense, giving 京 its meaning 'capital city.'

example.hanzi: 他下个月要去东京旅行。
example.pinyin: Tā xià gè yuè yào qù Dōngjīng lǚxíng.
example.english: He is going to travel to Tokyo next month.
example.fact: Tokyo's greater metropolitan area is home to roughly 37 million people, making it the most populous metropolitan area on Earth. The city was called Edo until 1868, when it was renamed Tokyo, meaning 'eastern capital,' after the emperor moved the seat of government there from Kyoto.

components.note: 辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過
夕 (evening/night) — the darkness that has fallen
亻 (a person) — someone moving under cover of night

example.hanzi: 我们决定在山上的小屋过夜。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen juédìng zài shān shàng de xiǎowū guòyè.
example.english: We decided to spend the night in the cabin on the mountain.
example.fact: In towns above the Arctic Circle, like Utqiagvik, Alaska, the sun can stay below the horizon for over 60 consecutive days each winter — turning an ordinary night into a stretch of darkness lasting more than two months.

components.note: 发 is a modern simplification of 發, whose traditional form combined a bow 弓 with a pair of legs spread apart 癹 to depict the instant an arrow is loosed.
That image of sudden release broadened over time into 发's modern senses 'to issue, to send out, to develop.'
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.

example.hanzi: 他的老毛病突然发作了。
example.pinyin: Tā de lǎomáobìng tūrán fāzuò le.
example.english: His old illness suddenly flared up.
example.fact: Solar flares are sudden bursts of radiation from the Sun's surface that can release as much energy in minutes as billions of hydrogen bombs. The most powerful one on record, the 1859 Carrington Event, was strong enough to set telegraph wires on fire and produce auroras visible near the equator.

components.note: 以's earliest oracle-bone form pictured a person bent forward, holding or working with an object in their hands.
That picture of putting something to use gradually abstracted into 以's modern grammatical senses, 'by means of, in order to, because of.'
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

example.hanzi: 以上就是我们今天讨论的内容。
example.pinyin: Yǐshàng jiùshì wǒmen jīntiān tǎolùn de nèiróng.
example.english: The above is what we discussed today.
example.fact: Mount Everest's summit sits 8,849 meters above sea level, an altitude close to the cruising height of early jet airliners before pressurized cabins became standard. The mountain is still slowly rising a few millimeters a year as the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates keep colliding.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 挑 describes an action done with the hand, picking or carrying.
兆 (zhào) gives a sound distantly related to tiāo, having drifted apart over time.
辶 (to walk/move) — 选 relates to the process of selecting, as if moving through options
先 (xiān) gives a sound close to 选's reading xuǎn

example.hanzi: 她花了很长时间挑选礼物。
example.pinyin: Tā huāle hěn cháng shíjiān tiāoxuǎn lǐwù.
example.english: She spent a long time choosing a gift.
example.fact: Natural selection, the mechanism Charles Darwin proposed in 1859, works by favoring individuals whose inherited traits happen to fit their environment. Over many generations this quietly 'selects' which genes get passed on, without any conscious choice ever being involved.

components.note: 才 (talent) — many talented people.
囗 (an enclosure) — gathered together in one place, giving 团 its meaning 'group, team; round, ball-shaped.'
纟 (thread) — 结 relates to tying or knotting threads together.
吉 (jí) gives a hint of the sound — 结 is pronounced jié, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 全体队员必须团结起来才能赢。
example.pinyin: Quántǐ duìyuán bìxū tuánjié qǐlái cáinéng yíng.
example.english: All the team members must unite in order to win.
example.fact: Emperor penguins in Antarctica huddle together in tightly packed groups of thousands, rotating positions so every bird gets a turn sheltered from the wind at the center. This cooperative strategy can raise the temperature inside the huddle to nearly 37°C even when it is -40°C outside.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/settlement) — represents a city or town.
余 (surplus, remainder) — the leftover waste a city produces, which must be cleared away, giving 除 its meaning 'to remove, eliminate.'
扌 (hand) — 掉 relates to dropping something from the hand.
卓 (zhuó) reflects an older phonetic connection that has faded in the modern pronunciation diào.

example.hanzi: 农民想办法除掉田里的害虫。
example.pinyin: Nóngmín xiǎng bànfǎ chúdiào tián lǐ de hàichóng.
example.english: The farmer tried to find a way to eliminate the pests in the field.
example.fact: Smallpox is the only human disease ever fully eradicated worldwide, declared eliminated by the World Health Organization in 1980 after a global vaccination campaign that lasted more than a decade.

components.note: 攵 (a hand taking action) — 救 describes the act of rescuing someone.
求 (qiú) gives a sound close to jiù, sharing a similar rhyme.
扌 (hand) — 援 describes reaching out to help someone by hand.
爰 depicts one hand passing something to another, reinforcing the idea of lending aid — together giving 援 its meaning 'to help, to aid.'

example.hanzi: 救援队连夜赶到了灾区。
example.pinyin: Jiùyuán duì liányè gǎndào le zāiqū.
example.english: The rescue team rushed to the disaster area overnight.
example.fact: The 2010 rescue of 33 Chilean miners trapped half a mile underground at the San José mine took 69 days and required drilling an entirely new escape shaft. All 33 men survived, making it one of the most successful mine rescues in history.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 这个故事的开头非常吸引人。
example.pinyin: Zhège gùshì de kāitóu fēicháng xīyǐn rén.
example.english: The beginning of this story is very engaging.
example.fact: The Big Bang theory holds that the observable universe began expanding from an extremely hot, dense state roughly 13.8 billion years ago. The faint microwave radiation left over from that beginning, the cosmic microwave background, can still be detected filling all of space today.

components.note: A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
木 (wood) — early models and molds were often carved from wood
莫 (mò) gives a sound close to 模's reading mó, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
木 (tree/wood) — 样 originally referred to a kind of tree, later broadening to mean 'kind, appearance, way.'
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — 样 is pronounced yàng, matching aside from tone.

example.hanzi: 这两件衣服看起来一模一样。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng jiàn yīfu kàn qǐlái yīmúyīyàng.
example.english: These two pieces of clothing look exactly alike.
example.fact: Identical twins form when a single fertilized egg splits into two embryos early in development, so they share nearly 100% of their DNA. Yet even genetically identical twins raised together develop distinct fingerprints, because those patterns form partly from random pressure differences inside the womb.

components.note: 入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.
口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.

example.hanzi: 博物馆的入口在大楼的东边。
example.pinyin: Bówùguǎn de rùkǒu zài dàlóu de dōngbian.
example.english: The museum's entrance is on the east side of the building.
example.fact: The entrance to Carlsbad Caverns in New Mexico is famous for the hundreds of thousands of bats that spiral out of it every summer evening at dusk, a nightly exodus that can take over an hour to complete.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 接 relates to receiving or connecting something by hand.
妾 (qiè) gives a hint of the sound — 接 is pronounced jiē, a connection that has shifted over time.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 新经理接手了这个项目。
example.pinyin: Xīn jīnglǐ jiēshǒu le zhège xiàngmù.
example.english: The new manager took over this project.
example.fact: When Steve Jobs returned to lead Apple in 1997 after being ousted twelve years earlier, the company was reportedly only weeks away from bankruptcy. Within a few years of him taking over again, it launched the iMac and later the iPod.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.
手 (hand) — depicts a hand raised above the eyes.
目 (eye) — shielding the eyes with a hand to look into the distance gave 看 its meaning 'to look, to see.'

example.hanzi: 很多人收看了昨晚的比赛直播。
example.pinyin: Hěnduō rén shōukàn le zuówǎn de bǐsài zhíbò.
example.english: Many people watched last night's live broadcast of the game.
example.fact: The 1969 Apollo 11 moon landing was watched live on television by an estimated 600 million people worldwide — roughly one in every six people alive at the time — making it one of the most-viewed broadcasts in history.

components.note: 讠 (speech) on the left shows this involves words.
秀 (elegant, refined) on the right suggests alluring words, giving 诱 its meaning 'to entice, to lure.'
心 (heart) at the bottom shows this is about a state of mind.
或 (perhaps, maybe) above conveys uncertainty, giving 惑 its meaning 'to confuse, to be puzzled.'

example.hanzi: 巨大的利润诱惑着投资者。
example.pinyin: Jùdà de lìrùn yòuhuò zhe tóuzīzhě.
example.english: Huge profits tempt investors.
example.fact: Deep-sea anglerfish dangle a glowing lure grown from a modified fin spine right in front of their mouths. Bioluminescent bacteria living in the lure attract curious prey close enough to swallow in the near-total darkness of the deep ocean.

components.note: 十 began as a single vertical stroke, likely a knot tied into a counting cord — an ancient tally mark for the number ten. A short horizontal crossbar was added later mainly to keep it visually distinct from the character 一 (one).
二 is simply two horizontal strokes stacked together — the most direct way to picture the number two, following the same pattern as 一 (one) and 三 (three).

example.hanzi: 一年有十二个月。
example.pinyin: Yī nián yǒu shí'èr gè yuè.
example.english: There are twelve months in a year.
example.fact: The number twelve has been used as a counting base across many cultures partly because each of a hand's four fingers has three segments, letting a thumb tap out twelve counts. That habit is part of why the day is still split into two sets of twelve hours and the year into twelve months.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 遭 relates to something you come across or run into on your way.
曹 (cáo) gives a sound distantly related to zāo, having drifted apart over time.
至 (zhì, to arrive) — carries 到's core meaning, 'to reach, to arrive'
刂 (a form of 刀, dāo) gives a sound close to 到's pronunciation dào

example.hanzi: 这座城市遭到了严重的洪水。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì zāodào le yánzhòng de hóngshuǐ.
example.english: This city suffered severe flooding.
example.fact: The 1883 eruption of Krakatoa in Indonesia produced a sound so loud it was heard over 3,000 kilometers away in Mauritius. The tsunamis it triggered killed more than 36,000 people along nearby coastlines.

components.note: A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'
⺮ (bamboo) — 箭 names an arrow, traditionally made from a bamboo shaft.
前 (qián) shares the rhyme -ian with jiàn, though the initial has drifted from q- to j- over time.

example.hanzi: 这枚火箭成功地把卫星送入了轨道。
example.pinyin: Zhè méi huǒjiàn chénggōng de bǎ wèixīng sòngrù le guǐdào.
example.english: This rocket successfully sent the satellite into orbit.
example.fact: The Saturn V rocket that carried Apollo astronauts to the Moon remains the most powerful machine ever successfully flown, producing 7.5 million pounds of thrust at liftoff — enough to accelerate its own roughly 3,000-ton mass off the launch pad within seconds.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — 胡 originally referred to the flesh under an animal's chin or throat
古 (gǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 胡's reading hú
扌 (hand) — 扯 describes pulling or tearing something by hand.
止 (zhǐ) gives a sound distantly related to 扯's reading chě, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 别听他胡扯,那不是真的。
example.pinyin: Bié tīng tā húchě, nà bùshì zhēn de.
example.english: Don't listen to his nonsense, it's not true.
example.fact: African grey parrots can learn hundreds of human words and phrases, but studies show most simply mimic sounds without grasping their meaning. One notable exception, a parrot named Alex, was trained by researchers over decades to demonstrate a genuine understanding of concepts like color, shape, and number.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 眼 refers directly to the eye itself.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 眼 is pronounced yǎn; the rhyme has drifted apart over the centuries.
田 (farmland) over 土 (earth/soil) — originally referred to a village or a measured unit of farmland, later extended to mean 'inside' or a unit of distance.

example.hanzi: 在她眼里,孩子永远是最重要的。
example.pinyin: Zài tā yǎnli, háizi yǒngyuǎn shì zuì zhòngyào de.
example.english: In her eyes, the child is always the most important thing.
example.fact: Human eyes pack about 120 million rod cells and 6 million cone cells into the retina, but rods and cones can't detect fine detail and color in the same spot at once. That's part of why very dim stars are easier to see by looking slightly to the side of them rather than straight at them.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 袜 (socks) are an item of clothing.
末 (mò) gives a sound only distantly related to wà today, a connection that has faded over roughly three millennia of sound change.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 这双袜子又厚又暖。
example.pinyin: Zhè shuāng wàzi yòu hòu yòu nuǎn.
example.english: This pair of socks is thick and warm.
example.fact: Merino wool socks can absorb roughly a third of their dry weight in moisture while still keeping the wearer's feet feeling relatively dry. The wool fiber's crimped structure wicks sweat away from the skin faster than cotton, which is why many hikers prefer wool socks even in warm weather.

components.note: 日 (sun, related to time) — 暂 describes a short span of time.
斩 (zhǎn) gives a sound close to zàn.
亻 (person) — 停 relates to a person coming to a halt
亭 (tíng) gives the sound — an exact match with 停's reading tíng

example.hanzi: 教练在最后一分钟叫了暂停。
example.pinyin: Jiàoliàn zài zuìhòu yī fēnzhōng jiàole zàntíng.
example.english: The coach called a timeout in the last minute.
example.fact: Tardigrades, microscopic animals also known as water bears, can enter a dormant state called cryptobiosis that essentially pauses their metabolism to nearly zero. In that state they have survived being frozen, dried out for years, and even brief exposure to the vacuum of space.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 做 relates to a person carrying out an action.
故 (cause, reason, to happen) — combined with 亻 (person), 做 came to mean 'to make' or 'to do,' someone actively causing something to happen.
氵 (water/stream) — water naturally follows a fixed course, an image linked to the idea of 'law' or 'method.'
去 (to go/a course) — the path a stream follows suggested a regulated, consistent way of doing things, hence 'law, method.'

example.hanzi: 这种做法很快就见到了效果。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng zuòfǎ hěn kuài jiù jiàndào le xiàoguǒ.
example.english: This method quickly showed results.
example.fact: The scientific method, formalized by philosophers like Francis Bacon in the early 1600s, standardized a repeatable way of testing ideas through observation and experiment rather than relying purely on authority or tradition. It remains the basic method behind nearly all modern scientific discovery.

meanings: to bear (an expense, a responsibility etc)

components.note: 人 — a person, shown bending over
贝 (money/shell) — a heavy load of money the person is carrying on their back
扌 (hand) — 担 relates to carrying something, often on a shoulder pole
旦 (dàn) gives a sound close to 担's reading dān, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 高昂的学费给家庭带来了很大的负担。
example.pinyin: Gāo'áng de xuéfèi gěi jiātíng dàilái le hěn dà de fùdān.
example.english: The high tuition fees brought a heavy burden on the family.
example.fact: Dung beetles are among the strongest animals relative to their size, with some species able to pull more than 1,000 times their own body weight — roughly equivalent to an average person hauling six loaded double-decker buses.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 惹 describes provoking an emotional reaction in someone.
若 (ruò) gives a sound distantly related to rě, sharing the initial r- but the rhyme has drifted over time.
广 (shelter) pictures a drying shed.
林-shaped strokes below picture hemp fibers hung to dry, giving 麻 its meaning 'hemp.'
火 (fire) — 烦 describes a burning, irritated feeling.
页 (yè) gives a sound distantly related to fán, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他总是喜欢惹麻烦。
example.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì xǐhuan rěmáfan.
example.english: He always likes to stir up trouble.
example.fact: Cane toads were introduced to Australia in 1935 to control beetles damaging sugar cane crops, but the toads couldn't actually reach the beetles. Instead they spread across the continent, poisoning native predators and becoming one of Australia's most damaging invasive species.

components.note: 人 (person), doubled — one person shown following another depicts the idea of accompanying or coming from somewhere.
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'

example.hanzi: 她从不迟到。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngbù chídào.
example.english: She is never late.
example.fact: Contrary to the popular saying that lightning never strikes the same place twice, it can and does — the Empire State Building is struck by lightning roughly 20 times a year, thanks to its height and prominent position in New York City.

components.note: 氵 (water) — sand forms as water erodes rock over time.
少 (shǎo) shares the initial sh- with shā, though the vowel has since shifted.
氵 (water) — a beach or sandbar is found at the water's edge.
难 (difficult) contributes to the character's form, describing waters that are tricky to navigate near a shoal.

example.hanzi: 孩子们在沙滩上堆城堡。
example.pinyin: Háizimen zài shātān shàng duī chéngbǎo.
example.english: The children are building castles on the beach.
example.fact: Much of the white sand on tropical beaches like those in the Caribbean isn't ground-up rock at all — it's largely the crushed skeletal remains of coral and shells, a lot of it passed through the digestive systems of parrotfish, which can each produce hundreds of pounds of sand a year.

components.note: 礻 (an altar, related to ritual) — 社 relates to worship and community gatherings.
土 (earth) — ancient communities worshipped a local earth spirit together, giving 社 its meaning 'society' or 'community.'
Depicts a person standing with legs crossed — the crossing shape gave 交 its meaning 'to intersect, exchange, hand over.'

example.hanzi: 他不太喜欢参加社交活动。
example.pinyin: Tā bú tài xǐhuan cānjiā shèjiāo huódòng.
example.english: He doesn't really like attending social events.
example.fact: Honeybee colonies coordinate almost entirely through a shared social structure, communicating the direction and distance of food sources to each other with a precise 'waggle dance' that other bees can read and follow to the exact location.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 烦 describes a burning, irritated feeling.
页 (yè) gives a sound distantly related to fán, having drifted apart over time.
忄 (heart) shows 恼 describes an emotional state, feeling angry or annoyed.

example.hanzi: 最近的工作让他很烦恼。
example.pinyin: Zuìjìn de gōngzuò ràng tā hěn fánnǎo.
example.english: His recent work has been troubling him a lot.
example.fact: Cortisol, the hormone most associated with stress, follows a natural daily rhythm, typically peaking within an hour of waking and gradually declining through the day. Chronic elevated cortisol from ongoing stress has been linked to disrupted sleep and a weakened immune response.

components.note: 着 arose as a graphic variant of 著 (zhù/zhuó), which paired 艹 (plant fiber) with 者 to suggest fastening or attaching something.

Its lower 目 (eye) component belongs to that later simplified shape rather than to an original meaning, and today mainly distinguishes 着's readings — including zháo, as in 着火 'to catch fire' — from 著's literary uses.
A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'

example.hanzi: 厨房突然着火了。
example.pinyin: Chúfáng tūrán zháohuǒ le.
example.english: The kitchen suddenly caught fire.
example.fact: Peat bogs can smolder underground for months or even years after a wildfire appears to be out. The dense, slow-burning peat traps just enough oxygen to keep combustion going deep below the surface, sometimes flaring back up long after firefighters have left the scene.

components.note: 车 (cart) — 轮 names the wheel of a vehicle.
仑 (lún) gives the sound — an exact match with 轮's reading lún.
⺼ (flesh) — 胎 originally named an unborn child inside the body.
台 (tái) gives the sound — a close match for tāi, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 这辆车的轮胎需要更换了。
example.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē de lúntāi xūyào gēnghuàn le.
example.english: This car's tires need to be replaced.
example.fact: Vulcanization, the process that turns soft natural rubber into the durable, elastic material used in tires, was discovered by Charles Goodyear in 1839 after he accidentally left a rubber-sulfur mixture on a hot stove. It remains the basic chemical process behind virtually every rubber tire made today.

components.note: 禾 (grain, a growing stalk) — 移's original meaning was transplanting rice seedlings from a nursery bed.
多 (many, much) pictures repeated stalks moved together, reinforcing the idea of shifting many plants at once — later generalized into 移's modern meaning 'to move, to shift, to migrate.'
巳 (here representing an eye) — in one traditional theory, this depicted a captive's marked eye, an ancient sign of subjugation, which later broadened to mean 'the common people.'
戈 (a dagger-axe) — combined with the eye shape above, this ties the character to the idea of marking or piercing.

example.hanzi: 他们全家决定移民到加拿大。
example.pinyin: Tāmen quánjiā juédìng yímín dào Jiānádà.
example.english: Their whole family decided to immigrate to Canada.
example.fact: The Arctic tern makes one of the longest migrations of any animal, flying roughly 70,000 kilometers a year between its Arctic breeding grounds and Antarctic feeding waters. Over its lifetime it can cover a distance equivalent to going to the Moon and back several times.

components.note: 才 (talent) — many talented people.
囗 (an enclosure) — gathered together in one place, giving 团 its meaning 'group, team; round, ball-shaped.'
亻 (person) — 体 refers to the human body.
本 (root, foundation) beside the person suggests the body as one's basic foundation; this simplified pairing replaced the far more complex traditional form 體, which combined 骨 (bone) with 豊.

example.hanzi: 这个团体经常组织公益活动。
example.pinyin: Zhège tuántǐ jīngcháng zǔzhī gōngyì huódòng.
example.english: This organization often organizes charity events.
example.fact: Sardines and other schooling fish swim in tightly coordinated groups of thousands or even millions. The formation confuses predators and can shift shape almost instantly, because each fish is simply reacting to the movement of its nearest neighbors.

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'

example.hanzi: 他慢慢地从楼下走了上来。
example.pinyin: Tā mànmàn de cóng lóuxià zǒule shànglái.
example.english: He slowly walked up from downstairs.
example.fact: Old Faithful, the famous geyser in Yellowstone National Park, has been erupting fairly predictably for well over a century, sending water and steam surging up to 55 meters into the air roughly every 60 to 110 minutes.

components.note: 月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.
用's ancient bronze-script form is thought to picture a wooden bucket, pail, or possibly a ritual vessel — an object put to practical use, which gave the character its meaning 'to use, to employ.'

example.hanzi: 这个工具在旅行中非常有用。
example.pinyin: Zhège gōngjù zài lǚxíng zhōng fēicháng yǒuyòng.
example.english: This tool is very useful while traveling.
example.fact: Spider silk is, by weight, stronger than steel and tougher than Kevlar. Scientists have long tried to harvest or synthesize it at scale because of how broadly useful a fiber this strong, lightweight, and biodegradable could be.

components.note: 寸 (a hand) reaching for 旦 (originally 貝, a shell used as currency) — a picture of grasping something valuable, hence 'to obtain, to get.'
Depicts a child wrapped in swaddling, related to 子 (child); the picture-meaning has nothing to do with its modern grammatical role marking a completed action or change of state.

example.hanzi: 得了,别再说了。
example.pinyin: Déle, bié zài shuō le.
example.english: All right, that's enough, stop talking about it.
example.fact: Leptin is a hormone released by fat cells that signals to the brain when the body has had enough food, helping regulate appetite. Mice bred without the ability to produce leptin keep eating well past the point other mice would stop, growing severely obese as a result.

meanings: to snatch (esp related to a robbery)

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 抢 describes seizing or grabbing something forcefully.
仓 (cāng) is only distantly related in sound to qiǎng — both end in the -ang family, but the initial and tone have drifted apart.
土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.

example.hanzi: 小偷抢走了她的钱包。
example.pinyin: Xiǎotōu qiǎngzǒu le tā de qiánbāo.
example.english: The thief snatched her wallet.
example.fact: Some seabirds, like skuas and frigatebirds, practice kleptoparasitism — rather than catching their own fish, they harass other birds mid-flight until they drop or regurgitate their catch, then swoop in to snatch the stolen meal.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 查's original meaning was a raft made of lashed-together logs used to cross water.
旦 (dàn) supplies a sound related to zhā, an early reading of 查 before it was borrowed for its now-common meaning 'to check, to inspect.'

尔 simplifies 爾, whose ancient form is thought to have pictured a decorative window lattice or a bundle tied with cord. The shape was borrowed early on purely for its sound to write the second-person pronoun 'you' and the demonstrative 'that.'
斤 (an axe) — 斯's original meaning was 'to split apart, to chop,' the action of cutting something with an axe.
其 (qí) supplies a sound related to sī; the character was later borrowed mainly for that sound to write the demonstrative 'this' and syllables in transliterated names like 查尔斯.

example.hanzi: 查尔斯是我最好的朋友。
example.pinyin: Chá'ěrsī shì wǒ zuì hǎo de péngyou.
example.english: Charles is my best friend.
example.fact: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine in the 1830s, a mechanical, programmable computer powered by steam and using punched cards for input. It was never fully built in his lifetime, but working models constructed from his surviving plans in the 1990s proved the design would have worked.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 举 relates to lifting or raising something with the hand
舉 (jǔ) is the traditional character's own form, giving the sound directly, an exact match
力 (strength) — relates to 办's meaning 'to handle, manage, do,' something accomplished through effort.
八 (bā) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from bàn.

example.hanzi: 这座城市将举办一场国际比赛。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì jiāng jǔbàn yī chǎng guójì bǐsài.
example.english: This city will hold an international competition.
example.fact: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896, reviving a tradition from ancient Greece that had lapsed for roughly 1,500 years. Only 14 nations and around 241 athletes took part, compared to the thousands who compete today.

components.note: 目 (eye) — 眼 refers directly to the eye itself.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 眼 is pronounced yǎn; the rhyme has drifted apart over the centuries.
氵 (water) — the liquid falling.
目 (eye) — together showing water falling from the eyes, giving 泪 its meaning 'tears.'

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息,她忍不住流下了眼泪。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā rěnbuzhù liúxià le yǎnlèi.
example.english: Upon hearing this news, she couldn't help but shed tears.
example.fact: Human tears actually come in three distinct types: basal tears that keep the eye moist, reflex tears triggered by irritants like onion fumes, and emotional tears, which are chemically different from the other two and contain higher levels of stress hormones and natural painkillers.

components.note: 彳 (a road/step) — someone arriving on the road
寺 (a court/hall) — the destination where the visitor is welcomed
令 (an order, command) — 命 pictures issuing a command.
口 (mouth) — a command given aloud gave 命 its meaning 'order' or 'decree,' and by extension, 'fate' or 'life.'

example.hanzi: 医疗队随时待命,准备出发。
example.pinyin: Yīliáo duì suíshí dàimìng, zhǔnbèi chūfā.
example.english: The medical team is on standby at all times, ready to leave.
example.fact: Backup generators at hospitals are kept fueled and tested regularly so they can switch on within seconds of a power outage. Operating rooms and intensive care units depend on an uninterrupted electricity supply to keep patients on ventilators and monitors safe.

components.note: 关 simplifies 關, whose traditional form paired the gate radical 門 with a crossed-bar shape depicting the wooden bolt that seals a gate shut.
Losing the gate radical, 关 keeps just that crossed-bar image, carrying forward the meanings 'to close, to shut' and, by extension, 'a link, a connection' as in 关联.
耳 (ear) — 联 originally meant 'connected, linked,' perhaps through the image of joined loops.
关 (guān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lián.

example.hanzi: 这两个事件之间有很大的关联。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè shìjiàn zhījiān yǒu hěn dà de guānlián.
example.english: There is a strong connection between these two events.
example.fact: Many forest trees are physically connected underground through mycorrhizal fungal networks, sometimes called the 'wood wide web.' These networks can link the roots of different trees and even different species, letting them share nutrients and warning signals about pests.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 倾 describes a person or thing tilting or leaning.
顷 (qǐng) gives a sound close to qīng, differing only in tone.
向's earliest form pictured a building with a window opening in one of its walls.
A window lets you look and face a particular way, which gave 向 its meaning 'to face, to turn toward, direction.'

example.hanzi: 年轻人越来越有网购的倾向。
example.pinyin: Niánqīngrén yuè lái yuè yǒu wǎnggòu de qīngxiàng.
example.english: Young people increasingly have a tendency to shop online.
example.fact: Confirmation bias, first named by psychologist Peter Wason in the 1960s, describes a well-documented tendency for people to search for and favor information that confirms what they already believe, while overlooking evidence that contradicts it.

components.note: 日 depicts the sun as a circle with a dot or short stroke inside — a simplified picture of the sun's disc, later squared off in the standard script.
月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.

example.hanzi: 请确认一下会议的日期。
example.pinyin: Qǐng quèrèn yíxià huìyì de rìqī.
example.english: Please confirm the date of the meeting.
example.fact: The Gregorian calendar, introduced by Pope Gregory XIII in 1582 to correct drift in the older Julian calendar, was adopted so unevenly across countries that Britain and its colonies didn't switch until 1752 — and by then had to skip eleven days to catch up, jumping straight from September 2 to September 14.

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赞 originally related to offering valuables in support of someone.
兟 (shēn) gives a sound distantly related to zàn, having drifted apart over time.
成's oracle-bone form is thought to depict a halberd-like weapon, possibly used in a ritual marking the completion of a task, such as finishing the building of a wall or settlement.
That association with finishing a difficult undertaking became 成's core meaning, 'to complete, to accomplish, to become.'

example.hanzi: 大多数人都赞成这个新计划。
example.pinyin: Dàduōshù rén dōu zànchéng zhège xīn jìhuà.
example.english: Most people approve of this new plan.
example.fact: Ancient Athenian democracy used a practice called ostracism, in which citizens scratched a name onto a broken piece of pottery called an ostrakon. If enough citizens cast that same name, the person named would be exiled from the city for ten years.

components.note: 戈 (a dagger-axe, a weapon) — 战 relates to fighting and war.
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — 战 is also pronounced zhàn, an exact match.
土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 这里曾经是一片古老的战场。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ céngjīng shì yī piàn gǔlǎo de zhànchǎng.
example.english: This place used to be an ancient battlefield.
example.fact: The Battle of Gettysburg in 1863 remains the deadliest single battle ever fought in North America, with roughly 51,000 soldiers killed, wounded, captured, or missing over just three days. The battlefield is now a protected national park studied by historians and archaeologists.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 热 relates directly to heat
执 (zhí) gives a loose sound connection to 热's reading rè
冖 (a roof/house) — the home being welcomed into.
友 (a friend) — brought close into one's home; the traditional form 愛 also includes 心 ('heart') in the middle — the source of 爱's meaning 'to love.'

example.hanzi: 他从小就热爱音乐。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù rè'ài yīnyuè.
example.english: He has loved music passionately since childhood.
example.fact: Wandering albatrosses can live over 50 years and typically mate with the same partner for life, performing an elaborate synchronized dance to strengthen their bond each time they reunite after months apart at sea.

components.note: 手 (hand) — 摩 describes rubbing something with the hand.
麻 (má) gives a sound distantly related to mó, having drifted apart over time.
扌 (hand) — a hand held out, palm up
乇 — something resting on the upturned palm for support
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'

example.hanzi: 他每天骑摩托车上班。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān qí mótuōchē shàngbān.
example.english: He rides a motorcycle to work every day.
example.fact: The world land speed record for a motorcycle, set in 2023, is over 623 kilometers per hour, achieved by a purpose-built streamliner on the Bonneville Salt Flats in Utah — a location whose famously flat, hard salt surface has hosted speed record attempts since the 1930s.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 保 relates to a person looking after or protecting someone, originally a caretaker holding a child.
呆 (dāi) gives a hint of the sound — 保 is pronounced bǎo, a connection that has shifted over time.
亻 (person) — the one settling somewhere.
主 (host, master) — the idea of a person settled in a place as if hosting it, giving 住 its meaning 'to live, reside, stay.'

example.hanzi: 他努力工作,终于保住了自己的职位。
example.pinyin: Tā nǔlì gōngzuò, zhōngyú bǎozhù le zìjǐ de zhíwèi.
example.english: He worked hard and finally managed to keep his position.
example.fact: Giant pandas were downgraded from 'endangered' to 'vulnerable' on the IUCN Red List in 2016, after decades of conservation work in China helped their wild population climb back above 1,800 — one of the more notable species-preservation success stories in modern conservation.
